Sam — attaching a concise canary procedure and an observability matrix. High level below, details in attached PDF/CSV.

Canary summary (short):
- Duration: 90 minutes (staging)
- Traffic profile: synthetic ramp to 10 RPS steady for 30 min, 60s spikes to 50 RPS for two 5-min bursts, then decay.
- Measurement windows: align p50/p95 to 1-minute rolling windows for detection, but aggregate to 5-min and 1-hour windows for contractual reporting.
- Gate failure conditions (example):
  * p95 > 1.5x committed threshold for three consecutive 1-minute windows
  * Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained over two consecutive 5-min windows
  * KV cache miss rate > baseline + 8%
- Rollback: automatic routing fallback to a compatible lower-latency variant; manual escalation to Redwood SRE on persistent violation.

Instrumentation notes:
- No proxy install required. We will use a short-lived routing policy and an optional X-Canary-ID header you can set from your load generator.
- Server metrics we’ll stream: per-route p50/p95, tokenized latency distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, in-flight requests.
- Traces: sampled 1% of requests by default; we can increase sampling to 10% for the canary window.

Attachments:
- canary_procedure_v1.pdf (step-by-step, 6 pages)
- observability_matrix.csv (metrics, retention, exposure)

Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference

Sam — following up on scheduling and the commercial ask. Two quick items: 

1) Scheduling: Confirmed for Monday, Nov 23 10:00–10:30 PT. Invite sent to your calendar. Please ensure your staging load generator can send the X-Canary-ID header; if not, we can inject it at the client side.

2) Commercial: We’ll provision the short-lived canary profile at no charge as part of the evaluation for NC-2026-483. If the canary shows we need a sustained reserved pool (Dedicated) to meet contractual p95 guarantees, we’ll follow the normal procurement path. For now, the intent is to validate measurement windows and instrument alignment.

If we see persistent tail variance during the canary that is attributable to customer request patterns (e.g., very high burstiness beyond the agreed traffic profile), we’ll capture that in a short post-mortem and recommend mitigations (burst policies, caching tweaks, or a dedicated pool).

Looking forward to the run — see attachments from Marissa for the exact gates.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
